set.presentation: A 28-year-old woman has 5 days of sharp left front chest pain that began after she moved furniture; twisting, deep breaths and lying on that side worsen it, exertion does not. HR 76, BP 118/74, SpO2 99%; pressing the 3rd-4th left rib cartilages reproduces the pain exactly.

A 15-year-old boy notes his breastbone has sunk deeper during his growth spurt; on long runs he tires and gets breathless before teammates and feels his heart race. Average height, normal arm span and eyes. HR 88, BP 112/70; lower sternum 3 cm below the rib margins; soft systolic murmur.

A 75-year-old man with 75 pack-years (quit 6 months ago) has coughed for 6 months; this week it is worse, with more, thicker sputum and breathlessness crossing a room; no fever. RR 28, HR 104, SpO2 87%; pursed lips, hyperresonant chest, faint breath sounds, long expiration, wheeze.

An 18-year-old college student has 24 h of fever to 39.4 C, shaking chills, cough with yellow-green sputum and worsening breathlessness. RR 26, HR 112, SpO2 91%. Right front lower chest: dull to percussion, increased fremitus, crackles, and bronchial breath sounds where they should be vesicular.

set.workup: Clinical diagnosis. If a neck film is taken: frontal view shows narrowing of the airway just below the vocal cords; lateral view shows a normal epiglottis and normal space behind the pharynx. Viral swab: parainfluenza.
